about: Marks as a MOTION: a plain jump, a jump under an operator (`d`a`, `d'a`), and a jump that extends a visual selection. Measured 2026-11-13: vim supports all three; nvi supports the operator form but not the visual one; busybox supports neither (it leaves the buffer untouched - marks exist there but not as motions), so the visual cases run vim-only and the rest vim+nvi. `'` is LINEWISE (d'a takes whole lines), ``` `` ``` is charwise and exclusive. The engine serves all three from one definition (Engine._markMotion), because the same motion has to work for a jump, an operator and a selection.

cases.name: a plain mark jump in normal mode
d`a deletes back to the mark, excluding its character
d'a is linewise, so whole lines go
d`a forwards to a later mark
y`a yanks to the mark and leaves the cursor at its start
v then `a extends the selection to the mark, and d takes it
v then 'a extends the selection to the mark's line
V then a mark jump stays linewise
